Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. - Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

2. What triggers recomputation (create, update, etc.)
3. What properties are extracted (e.g., title, snippet, summary, etc.)

Now I have a comprehensive picture. Let me compile the findings.

---

Here is a thorough report of all code related to memo metadata that is derived/computed from memo content in this repository.

## 1. WHERE MEMO METADATA IS COMPUTED FROM CONTENT

There are three distinct derived/computed metadata systems:

### A. Payload Properties & Tags (persisted in DB)

The core extraction engine is the **markdown service** at:
- `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`

The `ExtractAll()` method (line 356) performs a single AST walk over the markdown content and extracts:

**`MemoPayload_Property`** (defined in `/bench/home/work/proto/store/memo.proto`, lines 15-22):
- **`has_link`** (bool) -- set `true` when the AST contains a `gast.KindLink` node (markdown links)
- **`has_task_list`** (bool) -- set `true` when the AST contains a `east.KindTaskCheckBox` node (GFM task lists)
- **`has_code`** (bool) -- set `true` when the AST contains `gast.KindCodeBlock`, `gast.KindFencedCodeBlock`, or `gast.KindCodeSpan` nodes
- **`has_incomplete_tasks`** (bool) -- set `true` when a `TaskCheckBox` has `IsChecked == false`
- **`title`** (string) -- extracted from the first block-level child of the document if it is an H1 heading. The plain text is extracted recursively from the heading node via `extractHeadingText()` (line 173).

**`tags`** (repeated string) -- all `#tag` nodes found in the content (using the custom tag parser extension at `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/extensions/tag.go`), deduplicated while preserving case. Tags inside links/images are skipped (see `isTagNodeInLinkOrImage()`, line 122).

**`mentions`** (repeated string) -- all `@mention` nodes found in content (using the mention parser extension at `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/extensions/mention.go`), lowercased and deduplicated. These are used for notification dispatch rather than stored in the payload.

The actual persistence happens in the `RebuildMemoPayload()` function at:
- `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` (line 74)

This function calls `markdownService.ExtractAll()` and writes the results to `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property`.

### B. Snippet (computed at read time, NOT persisted)

The **snippet** is a plain-text summary generated from memo content via `GenerateSnippet()` in:
- `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go` (line 264)

It walks the AST, extracts text from `Text`, `AutoLink`, and `TagNode` nodes, skips code blocks (fenced and indented), adds spaces between block elements (paragraphs, headings, list items, table cells), and truncates at a word boundary with `" ..."` appended.

The snippet is generated on the fly during API response conversion (NOT stored in DB). The `getMemoContentSnippet()` function at:
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` (line 83)

calls `GenerateSnippet()` with a max length of **64 characters**.

The snippet is set on the API response `Memo.Snippet` field (marked `OUTPUT_ONLY` in the proto at `/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`, line 266) during conversion in:
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` (line 76-80)

### C. RSS Title (computed at read time, NOT persisted)

The RSS feed generates an item title from memo content using a separate, simpler method in:
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go` (line 302, `generateItemTitle()`)

This extracts the first line, strips markdown heading syntax via regex, truncates at 100 characters at a word boundary, and falls back to "Memo" if empty.

---

## 2. WHAT TRIGGERS RECOMPUTATION

### On Memo Create
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 108:
  ```go
  if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService); err != nil {
  ```
  Called before `s.Store.CreateMemo()`. The payload (tags + properties) is computed and stored with the initial creation.

### On Memo Update (content path)
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 447:
  ```go
  if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService); err != nil {
  ```
  Called only when the `"content"` field is in the update mask. The rebuilt payload is included in the store update.

### Batch Rebuild (all memos)
- `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, `RunOnce()` method (line 27):
  Iterates all memos in batches of 100, calls `RebuildMemoPayload()` on each, and persists the updated payload. This is available but is **NOT** invoked automatically at server startup -- the `server.go` `startBackgroundRunners()` method (line 153) only starts the S3 presign runner, not the memo payload runner. It must be invoked manually or via custom code.

### Snippet: On Every Read
The snippet is computed every time a memo is converted to an API response:
- `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators()` at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` (line 76)
- `batchConvertMemoRelations()` at the same file (lines 225, 248) when `includeSnippets` is true
- Notification snippets at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go` (lines 318-391)
- `loadMemoRelations()` passes `includeSnippets: true` for single-memo detail views (line 292)
- `ListMemos` passes `includeSnippets: false` for batch listing (line 297)

### RSS Title: On Every RSS Feed Request
Computed freshly each time RSS feed is requested, at `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go` (line 243).

---

## 3. WHAT PROPERTIES ARE EXTRACTED (Summary)

| Property | Source | Persisted? | Where Used |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`tags`** ([]string) | `#tag` nodes in markdown AST | Yes (in `payload` JSON column) | Filtering (`tag in [...]`), display, stats |
| **`property.has_link`** (bool) | Presence of `gast.KindLink` | Yes (in `payload` JSON) | Filter (`has_link`), UI filter chips |
| **`property.has_task_list`** (bool) | Presence of `east.KindTaskCheckBox` | Yes (in `payload` JSON) | Filter (`has_task_list`), UI filter chips |
| **`property.has_code`** (bool) | Presence of code block/span nodes | Yes (in `payload` JSON) | Filter (`has_code`), UI filter chips |
| **`property.has_incomplete_tasks`** (bool) | Unchecked task checkboxes | Yes (in `payload` JSON) | Filter (`has_incomplete_tasks`) |
| **`property.title`** (string) | First H1 heading's plain text | Yes (in `payload` JSON) | Exposed in API response via `Memo_Property.Title` |
| **`snippet`** (string) | Plain text from markdown, 64 char max | No (computed at read time) | API response `Memo.Snippet`, relation cards, notification inbox, map popups, webhooks |
| **`mentions`** ([]string) | `@username` nodes in markdown AST | No (used transiently) | Notification dispatch only |
| **RSS title** (string) | First line, heading syntax stripped, 100 char max | No (computed at read time) | RSS feed items only |

### Key file locations:

- **Markdown extraction service**: `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`
- **Payload rebuild function**: `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`
- **Create trigger**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (line 108)
- **Update trigger**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (line 447)
- **Snippet generation at conversion**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` (lines 76-80)
- **Snippet helper**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` (line 83)
- **Notification snippets**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go` (lines 318-391)
- **Store proto definition**: `/bench/home/work/proto/store/memo.proto`
- **API proto definition**: `/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`
- **Filter schema (uses payload properties)**: `/bench/home/work/internal/filter/schema.go` (lines 186-229)
- **Frontend filter usage**: `/bench/home/work/web/src/hooks/useMemoFilters.ts` (lines 73-77)
- **Frontend snippet display**: `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoView/components/MemoSnippetLink.tsx`
- **RSS title generation**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go` (line 302)
- **Tests**: `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown_test.go`

content.text:
h14.

**Computation site:** `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload()` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`, which calls `markdownService.ExtractAll()` in `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`. `ExtractAll` does a single AST walk over the parsed markdown content to extract all metadata in one pass.

**Triggers:**
1. **Memo creation** — called at `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` before the memo is persisted.
2. **Memo update (content field)** — called at `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`, only when `"content"` is in the update mask.
3. **Batch rebuild** — `Runner.RunOnce()` at `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` iterates all memos in batches of 100 and rebuilds each payload (available for manual/migration use).

**Extracted properties** (stored in `memo.Payload`):
- **`tags`** (`[]string`) — `#tag` nodes found in the AST, deduplicated preserving case.
- **`property.title`** (`string`) — plain text of the first block-level child if it is an H1 heading.
- **`property.has_link`** (`bool`) — whether the content contains a markdown link.
- **`property.has_code`** (`bool`) — whether it contains a code block, fenced code block, or code span.
- **`property.has_task_list`** (`bool`) — whether it contains task checkboxes.
